specAnchors.text: understand that the term transgenic means the transfer of genetic material from one species to a different species

primer.text: Not every GMO is transgenic. This note draws the line precisely: genetic modification alters DNA artificially, but transgenic status demands genetic material from a different species. Same-species edits make a GMO; only cross-species transfers make a transgenic organism.

modules.title: Drawing the Transgenic Line
modules.opening: The vocabulary of genetic engineering needs precision. Any organism with artificially introduced genetic material is a GMO, yet transgenic status requires the added material to come from a different species — so all transgenic organisms are GMOs, but same-species modifications stop short of transgenic.
keyPoints: Genetic modification artificially alters an organism's DNA to give it new traits.
Any organism with new genetic material introduced counts as a genetically modified organism.
Transgenic describes genetic material crossing from its own species into a different species.
An organism carrying DNA from another species is a transgenic organism.
All transgenic organisms are GMOs, while a GMO modified only with same-species DNA is not transgenic.

low.restatement: GMO means any DNA was added; transgenic means the DNA came from another species entirely.
low.analogy: Any renovation makes a house a building site, but only a foreign architect's blueprint makes it an international project.
low.examPointer: If asked to state the meaning of transgenic, say genes or DNA transferred between different species — no vaguer wording.

medium.restatement: A GMO carries any artificially introduced genetic material, whereas transgenic status demands material from a different species; the plant edited with its own species' DNA is a GMO only, while cross-species insertion produces a transgenic organism.
medium.analogy: A borrowed cup of sugar from next door makes you a borrower; a borrowed recipe from another country makes you an international chef.
medium.examPointer: Exam wording demands the species barrier: write between different species, not merely modified.

glossary.definition: Describing an organism carrying genetic material transferred from a different species.
Any organism whose DNA has been artificially altered by introducing new genetic material.
The complete set of genetic material of an organism.
